$comment: TinyG edge-next settings (Board settings spec §4). The write objects are the reviewed overlay that was packages/schema/src/overlays/tinygEn.ts, moved field for field (test/settingsGolden.test.ts). Ranges are the firmware's own checks where it has them (cited), otherwise a host bound (host:). Units are millimetres: every write happens under G21 (SAFETY §4.6 step 5). CODEOWNERS: the owner reviews every change.

groups.title: System
groups.explanation: Units and distance mode at power-up, work offsets and planes at power-up, optional stop, motor idle time.

groups.title: Board identity
groups.explanation: What the board reports about itself: firmware build and version, hardware platform and version, and its serial number.

groups.title: Communications
groups.explanation: How the board talks to Run: baud rate, flow control, receive mode, echo, line endings and the JSON and text formats. Run sets this itself. Changing it could cut the connection.

groups.title: Status report
groups.explanation: How often the board reports its state, and how much of the queue it reports. Run sets this itself. Changing it could cut the connection.

groups.title: Motor 1
groups.explanation: Which axis motor 1 drives, its step angle, travel per turn, microsteps, direction and power.

groups.title: Motor 2
groups.explanation: Which axis motor 2 drives, its step angle, travel per turn, microsteps, direction and power.

groups.title: Motor 3
groups.explanation: Which axis motor 3 drives, its step angle, travel per turn, microsteps, direction and power.

groups.title: Motor 4
groups.explanation: Which axis motor 4 drives, its step angle, travel per turn, microsteps, direction and power.

groups.title: All axes
groups.explanation: Settings that belong to no single axis: soft limits, cornering and arc accuracy.

groups.title: X axis
groups.explanation: How the X axis moves: its mode, travel, speeds and jerk, and its homing speeds.

groups.title: Y axis
groups.explanation: How the Y axis moves: its mode, travel, speeds and jerk, and its homing speeds.

groups.title: Z axis
groups.explanation: How the Z axis moves: its mode, travel, speeds and jerk, and its homing speeds.

groups.title: A axis (rotary)
groups.explanation: How the rotary A axis moves: its mode, radius, travel, speeds and jerk, and its homing speeds.

groups.title: B axis (rotary)
groups.explanation: How the rotary B axis moves: its mode, radius, travel, speeds and jerk.

groups.title: C axis (rotary)
groups.explanation: How the rotary C axis moves: its mode, radius, travel, speeds and jerk.

groups.title: Inputs
groups.explanation: What each switch input does, and whether the switches and the probe are normally open or normally closed.

groups.title: Spindle and coolant
groups.explanation: The spindle and coolant outputs: their polarity, and the PWM output that sets spindle speed.

groups.title: Offsets
groups.explanation: The stored G54 to G59 work offsets and the G28 and G30 positions. Set them from the Job view's zero tools.

groups.title: Overrides
groups.explanation: Feed and spindle override values the board holds in memory. They reset at power-up.

families.label: Motor {m} axis
families.description: The axis motor {m} drives.

write.rangeSource: EN config_app.c:1087-1095 (set_ma refuses an axis index of 6 or more, E112)
write.whatGoesWrong: A motor mapped to the wrong axis moves the wrong part of the machine, and a jog or homing move drives that part into its end stop.

families.label: Motor {m} step angle
families.description: Degrees per full step of motor {m} (1.8 for a 200-step motor).

write.rangeSource: EN stepper.c:1481 (E158: 0 or less refused with 108); host: at most one revolution
write.whatGoesWrong: A wrong step angle scales every move on the axes this motor drives: the machine travels further or less than commanded and can leave its envelope.

families.label: Motor {m} travel per revolution
families.description: Millimetres (or degrees, on a rotary axis) the axis moves per motor revolution: screw lead, or belt pitch × pulley teeth.

write.rangeSource: EN stepper.c:1499 (E158: 0 or less refused with 108); host: at most 1000 per revolution
write.whatGoesWrong: A wrong travel per revolution scales every move: a 5 mm lead entered as 8 makes every move 60% too long.

families.label: Motor {m} microsteps
families.description: Microstep setting of the motor {m} driver.

values.label: Full step (1)
values.help: 200 steps per turn on a 1.8° motor.

values.label: Eighth step (8)
values.help: The TinyG driver's finest setting.

write.rangeSource: EN stepper.c:1511-1530 (0 refused with 108, E158; from 450.02 any value other than 1, 2, 4, 8 is refused with a range error and nothing changes)
write.whatGoesWrong: The TinyG v8 drivers support only 1, 2, 4 and 8 microsteps. Older builds stored any other value anyway, so the scale no longer matched what the driver did; 450.02 refuses it.

families.label: Motor {m} polarity
families.description: Direction of motor {m}: 0 normal, 1 reversed.

write.rangeSource: EN stepper.c:1654 [0=normal,1=reverse] (set_01)
write.whatGoesWrong: A reversed motor drives the axis the wrong way: homing runs away from its switch into the opposite end, and soft limits protect the wrong side.

families.label: Motor {m} power management
families.description: When motor {m} is energized.

values.label: Off
values.help: Never powered.

values.label: Always on
values.help: Holds its position all the time.

values.label: On during a job, off after the idle time
values.help: Powered while a job runs, then off once the motor idle time has passed.

values.label: Only while moving
values.help: Powered while it moves, then off once the motor idle time has passed.

write.rangeSource: EN stepper.c:1535-1541 (st_set_pm refuses MOTOR_POWER_MODE_MAX_VALUE = 4 or more, stepper.h:266-272)
write.whatGoesWrong: Modes 0, 2 and 3 de-energize the motor when it is not moving: holding torque is lost, and an unbraked Z axis can fall under its own weight.

families.label: {A} axis mode
families.description: How the {A} axis takes part in motion.

values.label: Off
values.help: The board ignores moves on this axis.

values.label: Standard
values.help: The axis moves as programmed.

values.label: Inhibited
values.help: The position follows the program, but the motor is held at step 0.

write.rangeSource: EN canonical_machine.c:2756-2770 (linear axes up to 2, rotary up to 3; canonical_machine.h:287-293)
write.whatGoesWrong: Disabled, the {A} axis ignores its words while jobs and the preview assume it moves. Inhibited, its position follows the program but its motor is held at step 0: the next move of ANY axis drives the motor there, so inhibiting {A} away from 0 moves it back to 0, and leaving inhibited mode away from 0 moves it out to its position.

families.label: {A} maximum velocity
families.description: Velocity of {A} rapid (G0) moves.

write.rangeSource: host: greater than 0 (450.02 refuses 0 and below too, EN canonical_machine.c:2821-2840); 200 000 per minute is far above any TinyG machine
write.whatGoesWrong: Too high, the motors stall and lose position without any error; every later move is offset by the lost steps.

families.label: {A} maximum feed rate
families.description: Highest feed (G1, G2, G3) velocity on {A}.

write.rangeSource: host: greater than 0 (450.02 refuses 0 and below too, EN canonical_machine.c:2821-2840); 200 000 per minute is far above any TinyG machine
write.whatGoesWrong: Too high, feed moves can stall the motors and lose position; too low, jobs run slower than programmed.

families.label: {A} travel minimum
families.description: Lowest {A} machine coordinate: the soft-limit and homing-search bound.

write.rangeSource: host: a finite position within ±100 m (or ±100 000°); across keys tn < tm, at least 0.01 apart, and a range the firmware soft-limit test sees as one (float32, not fp_EQ, both ends above DISABLE_SOFT_LIMIT; travel.ts)
write.whatGoesWrong: A travel range larger than the machine lets soft limits and preflight pass moves that crash into the frame; homing searches that far before it gives up.

families.label: {A} travel maximum
families.description: Highest {A} machine coordinate: the soft-limit and homing-search bound.

write.rangeSource: host: a finite position within ±100 m (or ±100 000°); across keys tn < tm, at least 0.01 apart, and a range the firmware soft-limit test sees as one (float32, not fp_EQ, both ends above DISABLE_SOFT_LIMIT; travel.ts)
write.whatGoesWrong: A travel range larger than the machine lets soft limits and preflight pass moves that crash into the frame; homing searches that far before it gives up.

families.label: {A} maximum jerk
families.description: Jerk limit of {A} moves, in millions (5000 = 5 000 000 000 per minute³).

write.rangeSource: EN canonical_machine.c:2897 (E158: 0 or less refused with 108); host: at most 100 000 (millions), so the firmware never applies its divide-by-a-million path for values above 1 000 000 (canonical_machine.c:2900-2902), which would change the meaning of the number
write.whatGoesWrong: Too high, acceleration exceeds what the motors can deliver and they lose steps silently; a stop also takes longer to come to rest than the overrun bound assumes.

families.label: {A} junction deviation
families.description: How far the path may round a corner at speed on {A} (larger is faster).

write.rangeSource: host: greater than 0 and at most 5 (typical values are hundredths of a millimetre); 450.02 refuses below 0.00001 (EN canonical_machine.c:2881-2892)
write.whatGoesWrong: Too large, corners are taken too fast and the motors can lose steps.

families.label: {A} homing jerk
families.description: Jerk used when homing and when stopping at a switch on {A}, in millions.

write.rangeSource: EN canonical_machine.c:2897 (E158: 0 or less refused with 108); host: at most 100 000 (millions), so the firmware never applies its divide-by-a-million path for values above 1 000 000 (canonical_machine.c:2900-2902), which would change the meaning of the number
write.whatGoesWrong: Too low, the axis overruns its switch before it stops; too high, the motors lose steps while homing.

families.label: {A} minimum switch mode
families.description: What the {A} minimum switch input does.

write.rangeSource: EN switch.c:365-378 (sw_set_sw refuses more than SW_MODE_MAX_VALUE = 4, switch.h:42-47)
write.whatGoesWrong: A limit switch set to off no longer stops the machine at the end of travel. A homing switch on the wrong end, or on both ends, makes homing fail or drive into the far end.

families.label: {A} maximum switch mode
families.description: What the {A} maximum switch input does.

write.rangeSource: EN switch.c:365-378 (sw_set_sw refuses more than SW_MODE_MAX_VALUE = 4, switch.h:42-47)
write.whatGoesWrong: A limit switch set to off no longer stops the machine at the end of travel. A homing switch on the wrong end, or on both ends, makes homing fail or drive into the far end.

families.label: {A} homing search velocity
families.description: Velocity of the {A} homing search towards the switch.

write.rangeSource: host: greater than 0 (450.02 refuses 0 and below too, EN canonical_machine.c:2821-2840); 200 000 per minute is far above any TinyG machine (0 fails homing with 242, EN error.h:358)
write.whatGoesWrong: Too fast, the axis hits the switch hard and overruns it before it can stop.

families.label: {A} homing latch velocity
families.description: Velocity of the slow {A} move off the switch that sets the home position.

write.rangeSource: host: greater than 0 (450.02 refuses 0 and below too, EN canonical_machine.c:2821-2840); 200 000 per minute is far above any TinyG machine (0 fails homing with 243, EN error.h:359)
write.whatGoesWrong: Too fast, the home position repeats poorly from one homing to the next.

families.label: {A} latch backoff
families.description: How far {A} backs off the switch to release it while homing.

write.rangeSource: host: 0 to 1000; a negative latch backoff fails homing with 245 (EN error.h:361)
write.whatGoesWrong: Too short, the switch never releases and homing fails; too long, the axis moves further than expected after touching the switch.

families.label: {A} zero backoff
families.description: How far {A} moves off the switch after homing before it sets zero.

write.rangeSource: host: 0 to 1000; a negative latch backoff fails homing with 245 (EN error.h:361)
write.whatGoesWrong: Zero stays on the switch: a limit switch can then trip during the first move of a job.

inputState.labelSrc: EN switch.c:390 fmt_in; switch.h:55-57 swState (-1 disabled, 0 inactive, 1 active)

values.label: Off
values.help: The input is set to Off, so the board does not read it.

values.label: Off
values.help: The input is ignored.

values.label: Homing
values.help: Used only to find home. Pressing it at other times does nothing.

values.label: Limit
values.help: Stops the machine with an alarm when pressed.

values.label: Homing and limit
values.help: Finds home, and stops the machine at other times.

values.label: Probe
values.help: The touch plate input. One per board.

st.label: Switch type
st.description: Whether every homing and limit switch is normally open (0) or normally closed (1).

values.label: Normally open
values.help: The switch closes when pressed.

values.label: Normally closed
values.help: The switch opens when pressed.

write.rangeSource: EN switch.c:350-363 (set_01; E106); switch.h:50-51
write.whatGoesWrong: The wrong type makes every switch read as pressed or never pressed: limits trip at once, or never trip at all and the axis drives into its end.

sl.label: Soft limits
sl.description: Refuse moves outside the travel range once the axes are homed.

values.label: Off
values.help: Moves outside the travel are not refused.

values.label: On
values.help: Once homed, the board refuses moves outside each axis's travel.

write.rangeSource: host: 0 or 1 (set_ui8 does not check)
write.whatGoesWrong: With soft limits off, a G-code or jog error drives the machine past the end of travel.

gun.label: Default units
gun.description: Units mode at power-up and after a program end: 0 inches (G20), 1 millimetres (G21).

write.rangeSource: EN canonical_machine.c:3099 [0=G20,1=G21] (set_01)
write.whatGoesWrong: A file without G20/G21 runs in the default units: a millimetre file read as inches moves 25.4 times too far.

gdi.label: Default distance mode
gdi.description: Distance mode at power-up and after a program end: 0 absolute (G90), 1 incremental (G91).

write.rangeSource: EN canonical_machine.c:3102 [0=G90,1=G91] (set_01)
write.whatGoesWrong: A file that assumes absolute coordinates runs every move relative to the last one in G91.

mt.label: Motor idle timeout
mt.description: Seconds after motion stops before motors in power modes 2 and 3 are de-energized.

write.rangeSource: EN stepper.c:1602-1607 and stepper.h:281-282 (the firmware clamps to this range; the host refuses instead of letting it clamp)
write.whatGoesWrong: A short timeout drops holding torque soon after each move: an unbraked Z axis can fall.

spep.label: Spindle enable polarity
spep.description: Level of the spindle enable output for ON: 0 active low, 1 active high (the factory default).

write.rangeSource: EN spindle.c:62-81 (more than 1 refused; refused while the spindle is on or the planner is busy); config_app.c:1117
write.whatGoesWrong: With the wrong polarity, "spindle off" drives the output to the level an active-low relay or VFD reads as ON: the spindle starts when the app shows it stopped (SAFETY H11).

spdp.label: Spindle direction polarity
spdp.description: Level of the spindle direction output for clockwise: 0 low, 1 high.

write.rangeSource: EN spindle.c:62-81 (more than 1 refused; refused while the spindle is on or the planner is busy); config_app.c:1118
write.whatGoesWrong: The spindle turns the opposite way to M3/M4: tools cut backwards, and threaded tool holders can loosen.

prbp.label: Probe input polarity
prbp.description: Whether the probe input is normally open (0) or normally closed (1), independent of the switch type.

values.label: Normally open
values.help: The probe circuit closes on contact.

values.label: Normally closed
values.help: The probe circuit opens on contact.

write.rangeSource: EN switch.c:334-348 (more than 1 refused; refused while a cycle runs); config_app.c:1119
write.whatGoesWrong: With the wrong polarity the probe reads as triggered at once, or never: a probing move drives the tool into the work or the touch plate.

os.label: Optional stop (M1)
os.description: Whether M1 pauses the program. Session only: not saved, off after a reset.

write.rangeSource: EN config_app.c:668 (set_01); config_app.c:1120
write.whatGoesWrong: With optional stop off, an M1 placed for a tool check or a clamp move does not pause the job.

fb.label: Firmware build
fb.description: The build number of the firmware on the board.

fv.label: Firmware version
fv.description: The firmware version the build belongs to.

hp.label: Hardware platform
hp.description: The board family the firmware was built for.

hv.label: Hardware version
hv.description: The board revision. It decides which pins the firmware drives.
hv.reason: A wrong value changes the pins the firmware drives, so Run never writes it.

id.label: Board ID
id.description: The serial number the board reports.

ja.label: Junction acceleration
ja.description: How hard the machine may accelerate through a corner. Larger is faster.
ja.labelSrc: EN canonical_machine.c:3131 fmt_ja (prints only the length unit)

ct.label: Chordal tolerance
ct.description: How closely arcs follow the true curve. Smaller is more accurate and slower.

gco.label: Default work offset
gco.description: The work coordinate system selected at power-up and after a program end.

gpa.label: Default path control
gpa.description: How the board joins moves at power-up and after a program end.

gpl.label: Default plane
gpl.description: The arc plane at power-up and after a program end.

baud.label: USB baud rate
baud.description: The speed of the serial link to Run.
baud.reason: Run sets this itself. Changing it could cut the connection.

ex.label: Flow control
ex.description: How the board tells Run to pause sending.
ex.reason: Run sets this itself. Changing it could cut the connection.

rxm.label: Receive mode
rxm.description: Whether the board takes commands a character or a line at a time.
rxm.reason: Run sets this itself. Changing it could cut the connection.

ec.label: CR LF line endings
ec.description: Whether the board ends each line it sends with CR LF instead of LF.
ec.reason: Run sets this itself. Changing it could cut the connection.

ee.label: Echo
ee.description: Whether the board sends back what it receives.
ee.reason: Run sets this itself. Changing it could cut the connection.

ej.label: JSON mode
ej.description: Whether the board talks JSON or text.
ej.reason: Run sets this itself. Changing it could cut the connection.

jv.label: JSON verbosity
jv.description: How much the board puts in each JSON reply.
jv.reason: Run sets this itself. Changing it could cut the connection.

js.label: JSON style
js.description: Whether the board's JSON is relaxed or strict.
js.reason: Run sets this itself. Changing it could cut the connection.

tv.label: Text verbosity
tv.description: How much the board says in text mode.
tv.reason: Run sets this itself. Changing it could cut the connection.

qv.label: Queue report verbosity
qv.description: How the board reports free space in its planner queue.
qv.reason: Run sets this itself. Changing it could cut the connection.

sv.label: Status report verbosity
sv.description: Whether the board sends status reports, and whether each one holds only what changed.
sv.reason: Run sets this itself. Changing it could cut the connection.

si.label: Status report interval
si.description: How often the board reports its state while it moves.
si.reason: Run sets this itself. Changing it could cut the connection.

spph.label: Spindle pause on hold
spph.description: Whether a feed hold also stops the spindle.
spph.reason: Reserved on this firmware: the board keeps it and does nothing with it.

spde.label: Spindle restart delay
spde.description: How long the board waits after the spindle restarts.
spde.reason: Reserved on this firmware: the board keeps it and does nothing with it.

coph.label: Coolant pause on hold
coph.description: Whether a feed hold also stops the coolant.
coph.reason: Reserved on this firmware: the board keeps it and does nothing with it.

p1frq.label: Spindle PWM frequency
p1frq.description: The frequency of the spindle speed output.

p1csl.label: Clockwise lowest speed
p1csl.description: The clockwise spindle speed that the lowest duty cycle gives.

p1csh.label: Clockwise highest speed
p1csh.description: The clockwise spindle speed that the highest duty cycle gives.

p1cpl.label: Clockwise lowest duty
p1cpl.description: The duty cycle, 0 to 1, at the lowest clockwise speed.

p1cph.label: Clockwise highest duty
p1cph.description: The duty cycle, 0 to 1, at the highest clockwise speed.

p1wsl.label: Counter-clockwise lowest speed
p1wsl.description: The counter-clockwise spindle speed that the lowest duty cycle gives.

p1wsh.label: Counter-clockwise highest speed
p1wsh.description: The counter-clockwise spindle speed that the highest duty cycle gives.

p1wpl.label: Counter-clockwise lowest duty
p1wpl.description: The duty cycle, 0 to 1, at the lowest counter-clockwise speed.

p1wph.label: Counter-clockwise highest duty
p1wph.description: The duty cycle, 0 to 1, at the highest counter-clockwise speed.

p1pof.label: Duty cycle when off
p1pof.description: The duty cycle, 0 to 1, while the spindle is off.

spe.label: Spindle on
spe.description: Whether the spindle output is on now.

spd.label: Spindle direction now
spd.description: The direction the spindle output is set to now.

spc.label: Spindle state
spc.description: Off, or which way the spindle is turning.

sps.label: Spindle speed now
sps.description: The spindle speed the board is asking for now.

cof.label: Flood coolant
cof.description: Whether the flood coolant output is on now.

com.label: Mist coolant
com.description: Whether the mist coolant output is on now.

in1.label: X min switch state
in1.description: Whether the X min switch is pressed now.

in2.label: X max switch state
in2.description: Whether the X max switch is pressed now.

in3.label: Y min switch state
in3.description: Whether the Y min switch is pressed now.

in4.label: Y max switch state
in4.description: Whether the Y max switch is pressed now.

in5.label: Z min switch state
in5.description: Whether the Z min switch is pressed now.

in6.label: Z max switch state
in6.description: Whether the Z max switch is pressed now.

in7.label: A min switch state
in7.description: Whether the A min switch is pressed now.

in8.label: A max switch state
in8.description: Whether the A max switch is pressed now.

mfo.label: Feed override
mfo.description: The feed override factor asked for. 1 is 100 %.
mfo.reason: Changed from the Job view's feed override.

mfoe.label: Feed override switch
mfoe.description: Whether feed override is turned on.
mfoe.reason: Changed from the Job view's feed override.

m48e.label: Overrides allowed (M48)
m48e.description: Whether overrides may act at all. M48 turns them on and M49 off.
m48e.reason: Changed by M48 and M49 in a program.

mfc.label: Feed override in effect
mfc.description: The feed factor the board applies now.

mcp.label: Feed capped
mcp.description: Whether the board is holding the overridden feed at an axis limit.

mfe.label: Feed override acting
mfe.description: Whether feed override acts now: turned on and allowed by M48.

sso.label: Spindle override
sso.description: The spindle speed override factor asked for. 1 is 100 %.

ssoe.label: Spindle override switch
ssoe.description: Whether spindle override is turned on.

ssc.label: Spindle override in effect
ssc.description: The spindle factor the board applies now.

scp.label: Spindle speed capped
scp.description: Whether the board is holding the overridden spindle speed at its limit.

sse.label: Spindle override acting
sse.description: Whether spindle override acts now: turned on and allowed by M48.
